
# Elements of the DMS Plan

In this section, we will cover the following learning objectives:  

```{r, fig.alt="Learning Objectives: Describe the major considerations of a DMS plan, Identify the major elements of a DMS plan", echo = FALSE}
ottrpal::include_slide("https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/10nOR2t1-F0E01fItN_l8uYRWslH2PmebPvhQzCBeCPM/edit?slide=id.g3896feb580f_16_29#slide=id.g3896feb580f_16_29")
```

The NIH has provided an outline for what components of the Data Sharing and Management Plan are required.

The following are the questions that need to be answered in an NIH DMS plan:

1. Will there be maximum appropriate sharing of scientific data resulting from work supported by the award? (Yes/no.)
2. Will the scientific data underlying peer-reviewed publications be shared by the time of publication? (Yes/no.)
3. Will shared scientific data be made available for as long as data repository policies or journal policies require? (Yes/no.)
4. If the answer to any questions 1-3 is no, explain why. 
5. If scientific data from human research participants will be shared, will privacy of participants be protected?
6. List expected data that will be generated, including data type and repositories. 
7. For studies subject to the [NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy](https://grants.nih.gov/policy-and-compliance/policy-topics/sharing-policies/gds), will all large-scale genomic and associated data be shared? 

You can find more detailed requirements for each of these questions [on the NIH website](https://grants.nih.gov/policy-and-compliance/policy-topics/sharing-policies/dms/writing-dms-plan#preparing-a-data-management-and-sharing-plan). To aid in proactively planning for data management and sharing over the life of your research project, it may be helpful to consider the data types and size you plan to generate, the repositories available, and the corresponding budgetary implications before you begin your research.

## Overall Takeaways

<div class = motivations>
**Why this change?** As of January 25, 2023, the NIH is requiring all grant proposals include a Data Management and Sharing Plan to aid in the transparency and reproducibility of NIH-funded research. In May 2026, the Data Management and Sharing Plan format was changed, in order to minimize the administrative burden and increase efficiency. 
</div>

<div class = question_box>
**Does this apply to me?** This will apply to most NIH grants that create data (regardless of funding level), although some grant mechanisms and some data are exempt. **It is not required to share all data**, however a justification is required. Reasons not to share that are acceptable may be ethical, technical, or legal.
</div>

<div class = data>
**Where should I share my data?** The NIH has [lists of suggested repositories](https://sharing.nih.gov/data-management-and-sharing-policy/sharing-scientific-data/repositories-for-sharing-scientific-data), to help you find appropriate repositories for your data, as well as [guidelines for selecting a data repository](https://grants.nih.gov/policy-and-compliance/policy-topics/sharing-policies/dms/selecting-a-data-repository). If there is not an appropriate repository, you can share your data at an institutional (if available) or generalist repository.
</div>

<div class = money>
**How do I budget this?** You may request funds for data management and sharing as direct costs (including personnel costs). Infrastructure costs should only be included as indirect costs.
</div>

<div class = plan>
**How do I write my plan?** Your plan should follow the [required 2026 DMS Plan format](https://grants.nih.gov/sites/default/files/dms-blank-format-page-2026.docx), and address the types of scientific data that will be generated, the repositories that they will be shared in, and any limitations to data sharing. **You may be able to change your plan** in the just-in-time process or during regular reporting intervals. Changes require approval.
</div>

<div class = submit>
**Will my plan influence my grant score?** Although the Data Management and Sharing Plan is a mandatory part of most grant proposals, it will not be shared with reviewers and thus will not influence your score, however the budget will be visible to reviewers.
</div>

<div class = blackbox>
**Final Considerations**

The Data Management and Sharing Policy was introduced in 2023 and the Plan format was revised in 2026. The NIH has stated that they will learn from the process as it happens along with the scientists submitting grant proposals. In general, it's best to be mindful of what is **actually feasible** when it comes to managing and storing your data and try not overstate what you might be able to do.
</div>

In summary, DMS Plans require information about the data types you will generate, where the data will be shared, and any limitations to data sharing. You can use [tables provided by the NIH](https://sharing.nih.gov/data-management-and-sharing-policy/sharing-scientific-data/repositories-for-sharing-scientific-data) to identify an appropriate repository for your data. Remember that reviewers will not score you for your DMS plan.
